observations: Photo 0: one adult mountain bike, dark grey frame with neon yellow-green graphics, standing on a concrete yard.
Photo 0: front suspension fork with yellow-green lowers; no rear shock, so a hardtail.
Photo 0: disc brake rotors on front and rear wheels, rear cassette and derailleur, knobby-to-semi-slick tyres, a bottle cage on the down tube.
Photo 0: the frame has printed lettering but no brand or model is readable at this low resolution.
Photo 0: the number of gears cannot be counted; rust, chain wear and brake condition cannot be judged.
Only one small, low resolution photo from the drive side.

identity.kind: hardtail mountain bike with front suspension and disc brakes

claims.evidence: No brand or component names readable in photo 0.
Cassette and chainrings visible in photo 0 but too small to count.
Photo 0 shows a front suspension fork; there is no rear shock.
No clip of shifting or braking.
Photo 0 too low resolution to see chain, bolts or rotors closely.

risks.risk: Gears skip or do not shift through all speeds; derailleur bent.
risks.proof: Clip of the bike on a stand or ridden, shifting through every gear front and rear.

risks.risk: Disc brakes weak, rotors warped or pads worn.
risks.proof: Clip squeezing each brake lever while spinning the wheel, plus a close photo of each rotor and pad.
Clip compressing the front fork with hands on the bars.
risks.if_unproven: as a rigid fork needing service

risks.risk: Rust on chain, cassette and bolts; worn tyres.
risks.proof: Close daylight photos of chain, cassette, chainrings and both tyre treads.
risks.if_unproven: as needing drivetrain and tyre replacement

risks.risk: Frame cracks or dents, especially at welds and the head tube.
risks.proof: Close photos of the head tube, bottom bracket and rear dropouts from both sides.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic unbranded frame with cosmetic wear

risks.risk: Brand and quality unknown, which sets the price band.
risks.proof: Close photo of the brand name on the down tube and the fork and derailleur labels.
risks.if_unproven: as an unbranded entry-level mountain bike

proof_requests: Close photo of the brand and model lettering on the frame, fork and rear derailleur.
Clip shifting through every gear and testing both brakes.
Close daylight photos of chain, cassette, rotors and tyres.
Photos of the non-drive side and the frame welds.
response.reason: Photo 0 clearly shows a hardtail mountain bike with front suspension and disc brakes, identified by type, so it can be priced at worst case as an unbranded entry-level bike needing service. Gear count, brand and condition claims are unproven until close-ups and a working clip arrive.
